principles.text: Start from the channel you can reach, then a market where several players already win, then the idea.
All you need is one product people pay for and one distribution channel you can use again and again.
Validate with a landing page and a buy button; an MVP that can't charge money isn't viable.
Go B2B and raise prices: price is the easiest growth lever, and at high prices competition stops mattering.
Shotgun many cheap launches before product-market fit, then sniper on the winner until it plateaus.

sampleQA.question: I have no idea and no audience. Where do I start?

answer.text: Go channel, then market, then idea: ask where you hang out and who you can reach before deciding what to build.
Pick a market that isn't winner-take-all, with several players already earning what you want. If nobody else is doing your idea, that's a red flag.
Sell to businesses: at 200 customers a B2B product can make about $1M/year where his B2C product made $1k/month.

sampleQA.question: Should I build the product before launching?

answer.text: No. A landing page and a buy button can test demand before any backend exists.
He launched CyberLeads with a landing page and payment, then built after customers paid.
Launch in one day: warm outbound to friends, cold outreach to bloggers and journalists, then Reddit, Product Hunt and social.

sampleQA.question: My product makes a few hundred a month and growth stalled. What now?

answer.text: Spend about 90% of your time on distribution and only maintain the core product.
Run experiments inside the existing product instead of selling or starting a new one; he ran 20 within CyberLeads.
Pull the price lever: after niching down to agencies and adding testimonials he went from $29 to $99/month while conversions rose.
